Header: Pythium , Rhizoctonia , Fusarium spp. “Kinyaushi” or “Kiuno” in Swahili

Prevention: Avoid planting tomatoes in periods of heavy rains.
Avoid placing nursery in a shaded, humid place.
Select well-drained nursery sites far away from tomato fields.
Elevate seed beds to improve drainage.
Burn plant trash on the nursery site before seeding and incorporate the hot materials into the soil surface.
Or, in the dry season, cover the site with black plastic sheets for a week to heat up the soil and kill the pathogen.
Fungicide-treated certified seeds are of big help (e.g. copper oxychloride)
Alternatively, mix seeds with red copper during sowing.
Ensure aeration through spacing of seeds (>5 cm, 2” space) and staking of plants with wooden sticks.
Disinfect seedling pots and trays with bleach (=NaOCl)before storage.
Wear gloves or wash hands with water afterwards.
Do not over water because this favours the diseases.
You may only irrigate early in the day to allow rapid drying of leaves.
Monitoring: This disease is caused by different fungi that live in damp wet soils.

Search for areas of poor germination in seedbed, because this disease may rot seeds before or during germination.
Search for stem bases of seedlings with dark, water- soaked, soft lesions.
It is easier to prevent this disease than to control it.
When first symptoms appear, action may be taken quickly to prevent spread.
Direct Control: Uproot diseased seedlings and young plants.
Bury deeply, or put into plastic bags and burn.
Do not re-plant in the same spot
Switch nursery site the following cropping season.
